speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound results are normal, which effectively rules out De Quervain's tenosynovitis given the classic "mom thumb" presentation. Since nerve compression and tendon issues seem less likely based on your symptoms and test results, and considering your history of falling on an outstretched hand, I suspect a ligament injury such as a scapholunate ligament tear.
